name: VerneMQ
workload: EMQX-run Open MQTT Benchmark Suite, enterprise set, point-to-point 50K publishers : 50K subscribers at QoS 1 for 30 minutes, plus a 1M-connections-at-5k-connections-per-second scenario, on one AWS c5.4xlarge broker node with XMeter as load generator.
claimed_speedup: Sustains the 50k:50k msg/s target while Mosquitto stabilises at 37k:37k (about 1.35x higher sustained rate, derived from page data); 1M-connection scenario average latency 2.47 ms against Mosquitto 5.74 ms (about 2.3x lower, derived from page data). Latency is the opposite: 2136.62 ms average pub-to-sub for VerneMQ against 353.82 ms for Mosquitto and 1.58 ms for EMQX. Against EMQX 4.4.16 VerneMQ loses in every scenario (1M connections: 2.47 ms vs EMQX 2.4 ms).
hardware: AWS c5.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 32 GB), Ubuntu 22.04.1 amd64, all machines in one VPC subnet; CPU model not stated
tradeoffs: Erlang/OTP broker (needs OTP 27-29, libsnappy-dev and a C compiler for the LevelDB offline store), not C or C++. In the same benchmark it used much more memory than Mosquitto (6.30G vs 341M at 50K:50K; 22.4G and still rising at 1M connections vs 1G) and more CPU (91% vs 6%). Features per README: MQTT 3.1, 3.1.1, 5.0, clustering, shared subscriptions, LevelDB offline storage, plugins, load shedding.
caveats: Weak, mixed evidence; recorded because it is the only numeric head-to-head against a listed baseline that could be opened. (1) Vendor-run: EMQ sells EMQX, a competing broker, and runs the suite itself; XMeter is the load generator, the emqx/mqttbs repo holds only prose scenario definitions (no scripts), broker configurations are not published except Mosquitto persistence disabled, and the CPU model is not stated, so not reproducible (tier C). (2) The win over Mosquitto is narrow: VerneMQ only sustains the target rate, while its latency is far worse (avg 2136.62 ms vs 353.82 ms; p50 467 vs 361 ms; p99 16,500 vs 417 ms). In the 250K fan-out QoS 1 scenario both stall near 80k/s (VerneMQ 80k, Mosquitto 81k; avg latency 11,802.11 vs 12,240.83 ms); in the 50K fan-in shared-subscription scenario VerneMQ collapses (pub 7.6k, sub 3.5k, avg 116,888.61 ms) while Mosquitto reaches pub 50k, sub 40k (12,723.07 ms). In the basic set Mosquitto has lower average latency (0.25 vs 0.4 ms point-to-point, 5.73 vs 21.55 ms fan-out, 0.20 vs 0.34 ms fan-in, 0.6 vs 0.89 ms for 10K connections). The 1M-connection latency edge over Mosquitto is 2.47 vs 5.74 ms average with equal p50 (2 ms). (3) Old versions: VerneMQ 1.12.6.2 and EMQX 4.4.16 from the 2023 post; current VerneMQ is 2.2.x. (4) The repo README has only qualitative claims (high-performance, low latency), no numbers, and no benchmark is linked from the repo page. (5) Independent studies seen only as WebSearch snippets because mdpi.com, arxiv.org and koziolek.de are blocked from this container: Koziolek 2020 edge-gateway study reports maximum sustainable throughput VerneMQ 10K msg/s, EMQX 28K, HiveMQ 8K (no Mosquitto or RabbitMQ); the MDPI Energies 2021 stress-test paper is reported to put VerneMQ 1.11.0 first on QoS 1 latency in its cloud tests (copies disagree, unverified). A small third-party suite (lkskrt/mqtt-broker-benchmark) lists VerneMQ as considered but has no VerneMQ results. No number against RabbitMQ MQTT plugin was found. (6) Domain/category corrected from the Haiku guess (other-languages / concurrency-runtimes) to storage-and-data / message-queues-logs, where the Mosquitto wave-6 entry already sits.
found_via: seed-record pass: https://github.com/vernemq/vernemq README (no numbers), then WebSearch 'VerneMQ benchmark messages per second compared Mosquitto EMQX RabbitMQ' led to the EMQX blog 'Open MQTT Benchmarking Comparison: MQTT Brokers in 2023' (markdown source in emqx/blog on GitHub).
